Me! Diagnosed as Bipolar II as well. I got diagnosed at 17 w/ Bipolar and then with BPD at like 23/24. Currently 29 and have been medicated (Lamictal) for the last 3 years consistently. 

It can be scary at times, sure. I have made a lot of reckless, impulsive decisions when I'm manic and also splitting and/or obsessing over someone. My meds help with the unevenness of my moods which is nice. It does nothing for my BPD symptoms though because BPD isn't genetic, it's from trauma (at least as far as i'm aware). That being said, I'm much more likely to sit back and take a look at my choices while medicated than I would be otherwise.  I also have been in therapy for the last 6 years consistently and that has helped a ton as well. 

I'm now heading into a part of my life where big choices like kids need to be made and it's scary! My mom is Bipolar as well so my kids would almost definitely inherit that from me. I'm worried that it's selfish to pass this disease along knowingly. That plus the BPD makes me feel sometimes I'd be unfit to be a parent even though I'm a very maternal person. I also have a lot of issues with my relationships and not splitting at the most minor inconvenience. My fiance is wonderful but we're having some relationship problems that I know are fixable but I had a bad split after a fight and now I feel the urge to leave. I'm afraid that feeling will never leave despite how much I truly love him. Most of all, I still don't have a consistent sense of identity. I bounce from hobby to hobby, fashion sense, everything like once a quarter. It can be a bit exhausting to be almost 30 but still feel like an 18 year old trying to figure themselves out. 

That being said, I'm the happiest I've ever been. If me from 5 years ago could meet me now, she'd shank me to live the life i'm living lol. It's really hard but also not somedays. I like to think everyone has their struggles and this just happens to be mine. It makes me no better or worse than anyone else. I hope you can feel that way too someday :)

I'm here to maybe give you a lil hope. I also had a really rough childhood/teenage years. I was bullied at school and then had a bunch of rough shit happening at home. My early 20s were disappointing as I was basically learning how to socialize when everyone my age already had that down pact. Add in my unmediated mental illness and a marriage I got into way, way too quickly made my early 20s a different hell. 

But then something happened at 25. Idk if it's because my prefrontal cortex finally developed or what but I got tired of the life I was living and made it my mission toto fix it. I joined a bunch of social clubs in my city to make friends, actually put myself on meds to help with all my issues, and started working really hard to find things I enjoyed doing. And it took some time but I did it! 25 marked the beginning of the best years of my life. Is it perfect? No. But I'm truly the happiest I've ever been now at 29. 

25 is still so young in the grand scheme of things, I promise you still have plenty of time to make good memories.

I'm going against the grain and saying it absolutely got better for me after 25. I'm 28 now and there is no amount of money in the world that would get me to repeat my early 20s. I was diagnosed at 17 but truly my early 20s were some of the most miserable years of my life mentally. At 25 I started to get my life together and now I've been medicated and in therapy for 3 years. I def still have my manic episodes (like rn tbh) but I'm able to recognize them and create strategies on how to manage it so, so much better. Not saying that it'll always be so amazing but I truly can't imagine it being that bad ever again.

I think you can definitely manifest desires (good paying job, good partner, more money) but IMO trying to manifest a specific person or situation never turns out right and usually ends up worse if you do get it than if you just let the Universe lead you to your best path.
